analysis.title: China: Three things in China
key_insights: China October activity data showed a broad-based slowdown and missed market expectations. Industrial production, retail sales and fixed asset investment all decelerated.
The October weakness fits the recent pattern of soft activity in the first month of each quarter, pointing to a soft start to Q4.
Government-led investment has not picked up despite faster government bond issuance in recent months.
Individual income tax revenue jumped 90% yoy in October as offshore trust tax collections were remitted into the budget.
GS estimates the RMB120bn offshore trust related tax increase should raise full-year IIT revenue by 7.4pp. The jump is probably a one-off.

The broader trend of tighter tax enforcement, removal of exemptions and new taxes is structural and likely to persist. Possible removal of income tax exemptions on central and local government bond interest was reported in media.
The APEC Shenzhen meeting featured a trilateral Trump-Xi-Putin meeting on November 19 but no concrete deliverables were announced.
The BIS interim final rule of November 16 tightens Chinese remote access to advanced chips and servers. GS equity research says it will constrain China's frontier AI model training.

China has not meaningfully retaliated so far, consistent with its goal of accelerating domestic high-end chip development. Further restrictions such as the MATCH Act on semiconductor equipment export controls could trigger retaliation.
